outcome: Clinical risk index for babies (CRIB) scores

short-term neonatal morbidity (severe intracranial hemorrhage, cystic periventricular leukomalacia (cPVL), late-onset sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis, kidney injury and retinopathy of prematurity requiring interventions)
cohort: 255 very low birth weight infants born in two Croatian perinatal regions over a 3-year period (2014-2016).
finding: While infants born vaginally had lower gestational age, Apgar scores, birth weight, and higher CRIB scores, mode of delivery was not significantly associated with short-term neonatal morbidity after 7 days of life.
